To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new-generation Ozone Monitoring Instrument volcanic sulfur dioxide retrieval algorithm is introduced and applied to both the OMI and the Ozone Mapping and Professor Suite instruments, and that the new algorithm produces highly consistent results for both instruments.

we introduce a new generation OMI volcanic SO 2 product based on a principal-component-analysis algorithm, which shows improvement over the current operational algorithm in terms of retrieval noise, SO 2 retrieval bias, and consistency with other satellite instruments.

we have developed a new-generation OMSO2 algorithm that is based on a principal components analysis retrieval technique and that it is capable of producing highly consistent SO2 retrievals between OMSO2 and OMPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new generation of volcanic SO2 retrieval algorithms that are capable of producing more accurate SO2 retrievals and extending the data record well into future.
the development and application of a new-generation PCA algorithm for the retrieval of volcanic SO2 total columns from hyperspectral satellite measurements.
the development and application of a new-generation OMSO2 dataset for global volcanic SO2 monitoring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OMI SO2 product is the best available product for volcanic SO2 monitoring, and the new PCA algorithm is the best OMI SO2 algorithm.
OMI SO2 retrieval is a very good product, but the new PCA algorithm improves it significantly.
OMSO2 is a significant improvement over OMI L2 SO2 products, and it is a very important contribution to the SO2 data record.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully applied the principal component analysis (i.e., PCA) technique to retrieve volcanic SO 2 from satellite hyperspectral measurements, which is the most advanced approach for the current and future generation of satellite UV instruments.
the new PCA algorithm provides a significant improvement over the operational LF algorithm, and it is ready to continue the OMI SO2 dataset with the OMPS instrument.
we developed a new algorithm for OMI volcanic SO 2 data processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, with the right algorithmic design and proper treatment of the spectral fitting window, it is possible to obtain high-accuracy volcanic SO2 measurements from hyperspectral instruments with a wide spectral range and a coarse spectral resolution, which is a key requirement for future satellite missions.

, with proper treatment of instrument characteristics and the use of full spectral information, hyperspectral satellite instruments have the potential to produce highly accurate volcanic SO2 measurements.
the PCA technique is a powerful and flexible retrieval approach that can be applied to a variety of satellite measurements to obtain improved geophysical products.
